lesson.subtitle: Lesson 15 -- The First Morning
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato | Lesson 15 -- The First Morning
lesson.grammar_point: polite requests and permission with do you mind if I and would you mind + -ing

listenings.text: Morning Renato, it is Dave. I have already left for work, sorry about that, I start at six. Bev is in the shower, so help yourself to breakfast, mate. The bread is in the cupboard above the kettle and there are leftovers from last night in the fridge. Eat them, honestly, nobody else is going to. The wifi is written on the note on the fridge. Capital B at the start, then the dog and the year we got him. One thing. Do not use the small silver kettle on the shelf, that one is broken and it trips the whole house. Use the black one. And if you cannot find something, do not stand there being polite about it for twenty minutes. Just ask Bev. She does not bite. See you tonight.

Hi love, it is Bev. I am at work so this is quicker than typing. Two things. Dinner is at six thirty tonight, not seven, because Millie has training. If you are still at the beach at six, send me a message and I will keep yours warm. Second thing, the laundry. Do not do what the last student did and wash one shirt on a Sunday night. Put your things in the basket by the door and I will run it with ours on Wednesday. And one more. This morning you stood in that kitchen for ten minutes looking at the cupboards. Renato. Next time just ask. Would you mind showing me where the mugs are. That is a whole sentence and it costs you nothing. Right, I have to go. Six thirty.

items.situation: It is your first morning. You want a coffee and the kettle is right there. Ask your host mum.
Your phone is dead and your mum in Brazil is waiting. Ask for the wifi password and a charger.
You cannot work out the shower. Ask somebody to show you, without saying sorry three times.
Now you are the host mum. Renato asks if he can take the last of the leftovers. Say yes in two different ways.
Somebody asks: do you mind if I open the window? You are cold. Say no, politely, and say why.
